title: Lie groups, Part II: parabolic subgroups, Langlands decompositions and the Bruhat decomposition of real reductive groups
summary: Continue LieGroups Layer 9 on its carrier: strengthen the Cartan datum (invariant form, global Cartan decomposition), prove conjugacy of Cartan data with a fixed split centre and of Iwasawa triples, build the minimal parabolic P = MAN with its Langlands decomposition, the Tits system and Bruhat decomposition with cell coordinates, the classification of standard parabolic subalgebras and subgroups and their Langlands decompositions, general parabolics and the dynamical description, the self-adjoint matrix model pinned in Lean, and the comparison with R-parabolic subgroups of real algebraic groups. The abstract Tits-system parabolic theory is Tau Ceti's and is consumed.

layers.title: Reductive Cartan data and their conjugacy

targets.name: ReductiveCartanDatum
targets.statement: A reductive Cartan datum on G is a LieGroups CartanInvolution I G (smooth involutive automorphism θ with compact fixed set, reductive 𝔤) together with a symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form B on 𝔤, invariant under Ad(g) for all g ∈ G and under dθ = lieMap θ, with 𝔨 ⊥ 𝔭, B negative definite on 𝔨 and positive definite on 𝔭, such that the polar map K × 𝔭 → G, (k, X) ↦ k·lieExp X, is a homeomorphism (K = G^θ). These are Knapp's axioms (i)–(iv) without axiom (v).
hypotheses: G is a real finite-dimensional C^infinity Lie group (LieGroup I ∞ G, FiniteDimensional ℝ E), 𝔤 = LeftInvariantDerivation I G

locator.where: Ch. VII §2 (reductive Lie groups and their axioms)

layers.title: Restricted roots, positive systems and the two Weyl groups

targets.name: RootSystem.positiveSystem
targets.statement: For a finite crystallographic root system Φ (possibly non-reduced) in V: a positive system is Φ⁺ = {β : β(v) > 0} for v regular; its simple roots are the elements of Φ⁺ that are not sums of two elements of Φ⁺; Φ_ind = {β : β/2 ∉ Φ}. Theorem: Φ_ind is reduced with the same reflections, Weyl group and chambers; Φ⁺ ↦ Φ⁺ ∩ Φ_ind is a bijection onto positive systems of Φ_ind, simple roots are indivisible and form a RootPairing.Base of Φ_ind; W(Φ) acts simply transitively on positive systems; stabilizers of closed-chamber points (and pointwise stabilizers of subspaces) are generated by the reflections they contain.
hypotheses: Φ a finite crystallographic root system in a real vector space, possibly non-reduced

locator.where: Ch. VI §1 (root systems; non-reduced systems; positive systems and bases)
